problem.paragraph: Sketch the graph of $$y = 3^{x}$$ and $$y = \log_{3}x$$ on the same set of axes.

solution.paragraph: First, sketch the graph of $$y = 3^{x}$$ with the help of the following table of values:
Next, take the mirror reflection of this graph with respect to the line $$y = x$$ to obtain the graph of $$y = \log_{3}x$$ .

image.alt: Details Two curves and line are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis ranges from negative 6 to around 8 and the y axis ranges from below negative 4 to over 8 . The first curve y = 3^x enters the second quadrant, just above the x axis, runs parallel and veering off the x axis, rises upward, concave up, cuts the y axis at (0, 1), enters the first quadrant, continues to rise upward to the right, concave up, passes through (1, 3) and (2, 9) in the first quadrant. The second curve y = log_3 x enters the fourth quadrant, veering off the negative y axis, slopes steeply upward, concave down, cuts the x axis at (1, 0), enters the first quadrant, passes through (3, 1) and (9, 2) and bulges away from the x axis, which is the mirror reflection of the first curve. The line y = x enters the fourth quadrant, slopes linearly upward to the right, passes through the origin and (1, 1), and continues to rise linearly upward in the first quadrant.

solution.paragraph: $$\begin{array}{ccl} {3e^{x + 1} - 2} & = & 4 \\ {3e^{x + 1}} & = & 6 \\ e^{x + 1} & = & 2 \\ {\ln e^{x + 1}} & = & {{\ln 2} { \text{Take the logarithm of both sides} .}} \\ {\left( {x + 1} \right)\ln e} & = & {{\ln 2} { \text{Law} 3}} \\ {x + 1} & = & {{\ln 2} { \text{Law} 5}} \\ x & = & {\ln 2 - 1} \\ & \approx & {- 0.3069} \end{array}$$
